**[Medium] Defining `ATLY_APPFLOW_TEST_SHIMS` compiles 1,368 lines of previously-dead code for the first time, and no PR check builds the target it lands in.**

`ATLY_APPFLOW_TEST_SHIMS` is referenced by exactly two files on `develop` — `Steps/AppFlows/Root/RootViewModelTests.swift` (937 lines) and `Steps/AppFlows/Place Profile/PlaceDetails/PlaceProfileSaveRegressionTests.swift` (431 lines) — and is defined nowhere: not in `project.pbxproj`, not in `Base/Dev/Prod.xcconfig`. Both files are in the AtlyTests `Sources` build phase, so both have been silently excluded from every build since they were added. These four hunks are the first time the flag is ever set, so this PR is the first time either file compiles.

The flag scoping itself is right — all four configs are the AtlyTests target (`PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER = com.atly.AtlyTests`), and the two Release configs correctly take `ATLY_APPFLOW_TEST_SHIMS $(inherited)` without leaking `DEBUG`. The problem is coverage, not correctness:

1. `PlaceProfileSaveRegressionTests.swift` has nothing to do with guided first-session eligibility. It is activated purely as a side effect of a flag this PR needs for `RootViewModelTests`. It was last touched in `6272232a6f` and has never been compiled against any `develop` since.
2. `AtlyPRSmoke` is a fixed allowlist and the Xcode Cloud PR check builds the app product, not AtlyTests. So if either file no longer compiles against current `develop`, nothing on this PR is red — the broken test target lands on `develop` and surfaces later, to whoever next runs the suite locally or to the release regression job.

The local `146/146` focused run is the only evidence that both files build. Please confirm that run compiled the AtlyTests target with these settings and that `PlaceProfileSaveRegressionTests` executed (not just linked), or split the flag activation into its own PR so the unrelated file's revival is reviewed on its own.

*(Scope note, not a block: the `project.pbxproj` change is genuinely required by this PR's own `RootViewModel` regression test, so it is in scope under the usual carve-out — but it is worth naming explicitly, since the sensitive-scope gate is red on it.)*

— posted by the `aviad-review` loop (automated triage, not a human review)
open_findings.failure_path: `ATLY_APPFLOW_TEST_SHIMS` is currently undefined in the whole project, so `RootViewModelTests.swift` and `PlaceProfileSaveRegressionTests.swift` compile to nothing. These hunks define it on all four AtlyTests configs, so both files enter the compiler for the first time. `PlaceProfileSaveRegressionTests.swift` references `PlaceProfileViewModel`, `UserRepositoryMock`, `PlacesRepositoryMock`, `MapsRepositoryProtocolMock` and `userRepositoryMock.currentUserStateReturnValue`; any API drift in those since it was written is a compile error in the AtlyTests target. No PR check compiles AtlyTests (AtlyPRSmoke is a fixed allowlist; the Xcode Cloud check builds the app product), so that error is invisible on this PR and lands on `develop` green.

open_findings.body:
**[Medium] Putting `atlyPlusPersonalizationService` in the logout cleanup list also wipes quiz personalization on a plain same-account logout, which logout previously preserved.**

This correctly fixes the cross-account leak Baz raised, and I'm not asking to revert it. But it is a wider behavior change than the account-switch case it was added for: `LogoutServiceImpl` runs `eraseCachedData()` on every dependency for *every* logout call site — the side-menu logout (`RootViewModel` `.logout` notification observer), settings, delete-account — not just `.shouldLoginUsingToken`.

`AtlyPlusPersonalizationService.eraseCachedData()` clears `longQuizState`, `shortQuizState`, `likedSeeds`, `campaignHint`, the post-signup framing/welcome flags, and now the admission marker and consumption state. So an existing Atly Plus subscriber who logs out and logs straight back into the **same** account loses their quiz-derived personalization permanently — the long quiz is not re-offered to an established user, so there is no path to rebuild it. On the next resolve they get `.fallback(.missingLongQuiz)`, and anything keyed off `longQuizState` (home personalization) reverts to generic.

Baz's original comment offered two shapes: clear on logout, **or** scope the keys to the account (`namespace the UserDefaults keys by account/user id` / store the account id alongside the marker and invalidate on mismatch). The second one fixes the leak without the same-account cost. Was the blunter option a deliberate product call, or just the smaller diff? If deliberate, it's worth stating in the exec plan, because "logging out loses your Atly Plus personalization" is a user-visible change that isn't in #3490's scope list.

— posted by the `aviad-review` loop (automated triage, not a human review)
open_findings.failure_path: User completes the long quiz, subscribes, uses the personalized Home. They log out via the side menu (`RootViewModel` `.logout` observer -> `logoutService.logout()`), then log back into the same account. `LogoutServiceImpl` now iterates `dependencies`, which includes `atlyPlusPersonalizationService`, and `AtlyPlusPersonalizationService.eraseCachedData()` nils `Key.longQuizState` (and `likedSeeds`, `campaignHint`, `shortQuizState`). On re-login `GuidedFirstSessionService.resolveHero` reads `personalizationService.longQuizState()` as nil and returns `.fallback(.missingLongQuiz)`; quiz-derived home personalization is gone with no flow to regenerate it, because the long quiz is only offered during onboarding. Before this PR the service was absent from `cacheDependencies`, so the same round trip preserved all of it.

open_findings.body:
**[Question] Why make the cleanup barrier global rather than only on the account-switch path?**

Awaiting the erase loop is the right answer for `.shouldLoginUsingToken` — Baz was correct that `await logout()` has to be a real barrier there, and the new `RootViewModelTests` case pins exactly that. My question is about the blast radius of the fix rather than the fix.

The code you removed carried its own rationale:

```swift
// Was moved to the separate task as result of eraseCachedData()
// was visually noticable when doing logout via side menu
```

That backgrounding was a deliberate response to a real symptom, and this change drops it for every caller — the side-menu logout (`RootViewModel` `.logout` observer), `SettingsFlowCoordinator`, `AboutAtlyFlowCoordinator`, `DeleteAccountViewModel` — while only `.shouldLoginUsingToken` needs the ordering guarantee. The erase implementations are the same ones that caused the original jank: `MapsRepository.eraseCachedData()` fires `_managedMaps.send([])`, `_exploreMaps.send([])` and `updateFetchedMaps(to: [])`; `UserRepository` sends `meSubject.send(nil)` and `celiacSensitivitySubject.send(nil)`; `PlacesRepository` does `saveSubject.send(0)` plus five `setCodable` writes. Those drive SwiftUI invalidation synchronously, and they now run inside the window the user is waiting on.

Second-order: the loop has no timeout and swallows only thrown errors, not slow ones. `logout()` is now unbounded, and the new test asserts routing stays blocked until it returns — so a dependency that stalls no longer degrades to a stale-cache bug, it wedges the app on a blank screen. That risk didn't exist while the loop was detached.

Is there a reason to prefer the global barrier over awaiting only where the ordering matters — say, keeping the detached `Task` as the default and having `logout()` take a `waitForCacheErasure: Bool` (or exposing a separate `logoutAndAwaitCleanup()`) that `.shouldLoginUsingToken` calls? Happy either way if the side-menu regression was checked; I just can't tell from the evidence whether it was. Your call.

— posted by the `aviad-review` loop (automated triage, not a human review)
open_findings.failure_path: Judgment finding — no proven failure path claimed. The concern is that the documented reason for the original fire-and-forget (`eraseCachedData()` was "visually noticable when doing logout via side menu") applies unchanged to the four logout call sites that do not need an ordering barrier, and that an unbounded, un-timed-out awaited loop makes `logout()` a hang point that `RootViewModel` now waits on before routing.

open_findings.body:
**[Medium] The evidence still doesn't reconcile at this head — three different SHAs are cited and none of them is the current one.**

This is a follow-up on the reconciliation already requested in the 2026-08-02 review, which is not yet satisfied at head `e8af28c3`:

- The **exec plan** marks AC-1 through AC-5 `complete` and both Focused-unit and Native/XCUITest `passed`, all bound to "exact product head `b20d12fb`", with `last_updated: 2026-08-03`.
- The **PR body** still reads `pre-review focused/native proof: 125/125 ... at d179f2c2a7ac54ed3835284fd5fcf76188e36ebe` and `current review-remediation head: c9fa0ad0b16aeae7de690ce13a062779e0c771fc`, with "fresh focused/native/TestFlight revalidation is queued".
- The actual head is `e8af28c3d2e3c3214bf69b44d2decb1c2e4e0171`.

So the plan claims completion at one SHA, the body claims proof at two others, and no artifact is bound to what's actually being merged. The plan's own Verification table concedes the gap — TestFlight is `exact-head refresh pending` and Figma is `transfer pending` — while the Acceptance Criteria table above it says `complete`. Those two tables contradict each other in the same file.

This matters more than usual here because `AtlyTests` and `AtlyUITests` don't run on PR checks, so the local run *is* the only evidence that the central regression
(`testEstablishedUserWithMigratedQuizStateNeverReentersGuidedFirstSession`, now the ONB-005 anchor) holds. Please either rerun and rebind at the current head, or downgrade the `complete`/`passed` rows to name the SHA they actually cover, before merge.

— posted by the `aviad-review` loop (automated triage, not a human review)
open_findings.failure_path: No runtime failure path — this is a verification-integrity gap. The exec plan's Acceptance Criteria and Verification tables assert `complete`/`passed` against product head `b20d12fb`, the PR body asserts proof at `d179f2c2` and `c9fa0ad0`, and the reviewed head is `e8af28c3`. Because AtlyPRSmoke is a fixed allowlist and neither AtlyTests nor AtlyUITests runs on PR checks, no automated check re-establishes any of these claims at the merged SHA, so the fail-closed gate and its regression test are unproven for the code that would actually land.
